problem_text:
A logistics coordinator must allocate a series of fragile components into standardized protective crates for international shipping. The components and their respective masses are as follows:

* Component Alpha: mass 39kg
* Component Beta: mass 68kg
* Component Gamma: mass 40kg
* Component Delta: mass 60kg
* Component Epsilon: mass 35kg
* Component Zeta: mass 67kg
* Component Eta: mass 38kg
* Component Theta: mass 31kg
* Component Iota: mass 65kg
* Component Kappa: mass 38kg
* Component Lambda: mass 36kg
* Component Mu: mass 34kg
* Component Nu: mass 34kg
* Component Xi: mass 68kg
* Component Omicron: mass 37kg
* Component Pi: mass 42kg
* Component Rho: mass 36kg
* Component Sigma: mass 61kg
* Component Tau: mass 57kg
* Component Upsilon: mass 35kg
* Component Phi: mass 37kg
* Component Chi: mass 60kg
* Component Psi: mass 58kg
* Component Omega: mass 62kg
* Component Digamma: mass 40kg
* Component Stigma: mass 64kg
* Component Heta: mass 36kg
* Component San: mass 38kg

Each protective crate has a certified maximum safe load capacity of 100 kg. The coordinator must devise an allocation scheme that places every component into precisely one crate, ensuring the combined mass within any single crate does not surpass the load limit. The primary objective is to accomplish this task while employing the absolute minimum number of crates.
